block-definition.comment: Creates a new synthesizer module and gives it a name. The name is used by all other blocks to refer to this module. Creating a module with a name that already exists replaces the old module. VCO: oscillator (A-110). Inputs: pitch (1 V per octave, full strength), pitch 2 (scaled by the pitch 2 level knob), width (changes the pulse width, scaled by width level), sync (a rising edge restarts the wave). Outputs: saw, square, triangle, sine. Knobs: octave (-4 to 4), semitones (-12 to 12), pulse width (0-1), pitch 2 level (0-1), width level (0-1). With nothing in the pitch input and octave and semitones at 0, the VCO plays middle C. VCF: 24 dB low pass filter (A-120). Inputs: audio, cutoff (1 V per octave, full strength), cutoff 2 and cutoff 3 (scaled by their level knobs). Output: lowpass. Knobs: cutoff (Hz, the cutoff with 0 V at the inputs), resonance (0-1, sings on its own above 0.8), audio level, cutoff 2 level, cutoff 3 level. VCA: linear amplifier (A-130). Inputs: audio 1, audio 2, loudness (+5 V gives full loudness), loudness 2 (scaled by loudness 2 level). Output: out. Knobs: loudness (0-1, the loudness with nothing in the loudness inputs), audio 1 level, audio 2 level, loudness 2 level. Knob and inputs add up. ADSR: envelope generator (A-140). Inputs: gate, retrigger. Outputs: envelope (0 to +8 V), inverted. Knobs: attack, decay, release (seconds), sustain (0-1). LFO: low frequency oscillator (A-145). Input: reset (restarts the cycle). Outputs: sine, triangle, saw, square (-5 to +5 V). Knob: frequency (Hz). Patch an output into a pitch 2, cutoff 2 or loudness 2 input and turn up that module's matching level knob to modulate it. A module named "speaker" always exists. Patch into its "in" jack to hear a signal. Its only knob is volume (0-1).
Removes a module and all cables plugged into it.
Removes every module except the speaker, and silences the synth.

Plugs a patch cable from an output jack of one module into an input jack of another. Several cables may share one input; their signals are added. Signals and control voltages flow at audio rate inside the browser's audio engine. Example: connect osc1 saw to filter1 audio
Unplugs every cable from an input jack of a module.
Turns a knob of a module to the given value. Values outside the knob's range are clipped.
Reports the current position of a knob of a module.
Opens (true) or closes (false) the gate of an envelope module by hand, in place of a cable in its gate input. Opening the gate starts the attack, closing it starts the release.
Reports the names of all existing modules.
Converts a MIDI note number into a pitch control voltage (1 V per octave). Middle C (60) is 0 V, which is the pitch a VCO plays with no cable in its pitch input and octave and semitones set to 0.
